MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L15·N13736unmasked layer
This neuron fires on determiners/prepositions (mostly " the", also " for") that immediately precede a noun phrase repeating something already mentioned earlier in the passage (e.g. "handed **the** family", "**the** Xbox One version", "use **the** reclaimed door"), i.e. it marks the slot before an anaphoric re-mention; it is suppressed at sentence-final periods and similar clause-closing punctuation.

L20·N5016unmasked layer
This is a low-magnitude, largely non-semantic neuron that peaks at the syntactic pivot right after a subject/noun phrase — the copula/auxiliary ("is", "will"), infinitival "to", or the head noun completing an NP ("skills", "partners") — i.e., the point where the sentence's predicate begins, rather than on any particular topic; it is suppressed on similar function words in other contexts (e.g., the comma in "$25,000", "able", "drink").

Battaglia", tinyurl string), and is most strongly *suppressed* on the token right before an isolated capital "B" in abbreviations/model codes (z.**B.**, GP**B**, AR5**B**93, W**BS**), so it looks like a next-token predictor discriminating which capital-letter continuation follows.
